newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Castille-Leon grain outlook sapped by hail.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Castille-Leon grain outlook sapped by hail.

text.p: The barley and wheat harvest in Spain's Castille-Leon region is likely to be significantly lower this year after hail storms, the latest in a series of weather problems, a local farmers' association said on Thursday.
The region makes the largest contribution to the national soft wheat and barley harvest.
"The crop will be smaller this year. There was frost in May and more recently there's been hail, although wheat is more sensitive to this than barley," a technical expert at ASAJA told Reuters.
Hail damage affected 6,000 hectares in the region, he said.
ASAJA estimates that the barley harvest could be 20-30 percent less than the latest official forecasts for a 3.3 million tonne regional harvest.
Wheat may be up to 30 pct less than a government forecast for a 1.5 million tonne crop this year.
Continual weather problems in Spain, ranging from floods late last year, to a drought in late spring and now frost and hail, is also likely to delay harvesting, ASAJA estimates.
Instead of collection starting in mid-June, harvesting of barley may not start before July, with wheat ripening around one month later.
